title: ICU Language Access: A Practical Guide for Critical Care Teams
summary: Learn how ICU teams can manage language access across rounds, bedside changes, intubation, family updates, consent, goals of care.
body_markdown:
###


ICU patients may move between being alert, sedated, intubated, delirious, or unable to speak, while family members may also become major participants in communication and decision-making.


###


Use interpretation whenever a language gap could affect history, symptoms, treatment discussion, bedside updates, consent, family communication, or discharge and transfer planning.


###


The team should assess whether the patient can still communicate through writing, gestures, boards, or yes-no responses and provide language support for that method.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can support frequent bedside communication, rounds, family updates, and other ICU workflows when the system supports the language and communication remains clear.


###


Track time to interpretation, use during rounds and bedside changes, family-update interpretation, failed starts, ad hoc interpreter use, and whether language information survives shift change and ICU transfer.
